column1: # Batch 10 -- the em-dash tightening pass (D-22/D-23/D-24/D-25), through the unmodified
# committed sweep3.py rather than a bespoke classifier. The three starting patterns are the
# three D-23 measured: a spaced em dash with whitespace on both sides, a whitespace run
# followed by an em dash, and an em dash followed by a whitespace run.
# Two D-25 guards on every row, as lookarounds rather than a hand revert (a hand revert is
# re-broken by the next sweep run):
#   1. (?<=[^\s*]) immediately before the leading whitespace run -- requires a real preceding
#      character that is neither whitespace nor an asterisk. This blocks BOTH the column-zero
#      case (list-continuation indentation: no preceding character exists at all, so the
#      lookbehind cannot match) AND the run-in description-list case dashes.md still rejects in
#      tight form ("- **Reversible**--the choice", where the character immediately before the
#      dash is the bold marker's closing "*").
#   2. (?=\S) immediately after the pattern's own trailing whitespace consumption -- requires a
#      real following non-whitespace character within the SAME line. sweep3.py processes one
#      line at a time with no newline characters in scope, so this naturally fails at end-of-line
#      (nothing follows) and at line-start-with-trailing-content-only cases, blocking the
#      soft-line-break class where tightening removes the visible space on one side but the
#      renderer's own line-join still supplies a space on the other -- leaving an asymmetric
#      spaced dash the per-line checker cannot see because it never looks past one line.
